blocks.content:
• Highest court in India – Supreme Court
• Retirement age – 65 years
• Appointed by President
• Guardian of the Constitution
• Can punish for contempt
• Advisory jurisdiction – Article 143
• Basic Structure doctrine – 1973

items: Article 143 specifies the Advisory Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.
The Basic Structure doctrine was propounded in the year 1973.
Supreme Court judges retire at 65 years of age and are appointed by the President.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Supreme Court is the highest court in India and functions as the Guardian of the Constitution.
Judges of the Supreme Court are appointed by the President and have a retirement age of 65 years.
Article 143 grants the Supreme Court advisory jurisdiction.
The Supreme Court holds the authority to punish for contempt and introduced the Basic Structure doctrine in 1973.
